azk.review: Tarpor o dekhailam.. Je sir erokom e.. Grading valo dey.. Knowledge o valo helpful o.. Kin2 poraite pare na

1. do not miss classes.
2. do not write or explain too much in the answer script.
3. the shorter your answer, the higher your marks.
4. write only the key words and concepts. just show that you know how things work.
5. understand the core architectures, like how a residual block works in resnet model or an inception module in inceptionnet or how to count parameters of a feed forward network.
6. don’t worry about mathematical calculations or equations. questions are gonna be conceptual and theoretical mostly.
7. you can ask as many questions as you want in the class until your doubts are cleared. the lectures are not fast. easy to follow.
8. sir has vast knowledge in this field. he can truly fix your understanding of how DL works.
9. sir will teach in an organized and sequential way so you won’t feel lost.
10. use his office hours. sir is student friendly
11. never trust the sample questions sir provides before mid or final exams. they are only to warm up your brain; they will not appear in the real exam.
12. it is possible to predict some mid and final questions.
13. for projects, you can choose your own and discuss with him. if you have no idea, sir also assigns easy projects. you can even do a solo project.
14. sir won’t be strict about the project. choose a good idea, use proper regularization and optimization, show results clearly and submit a report.
15. questions are easy if you understand the core concepts.
16. sir really curves. easy going, easy grade.

That guy is only good for grading. You won't learn a thing from him. I did CSE495B under him back in 2024. He was very unorganized and unprepared. Coming 20-30 minutes late was his everyday thing, and he used to miss a lot of class. The funniest thing about him was his habit of forgetting things. He used to forget when the make-up class was scheduled, and thus most of his make-up classes were cancelled as well. He never uploaded the slides in time. I still remember I had to call him to upload the slides before the day of the midterm exam. On the midterm question paper, there were two questions entirely out of the syllabus. Upon asking for clarification, he told us he forgot the syllabus and mistakenly added those two questions (LMAO). Given that particular circumstance, what should he naturally do after that? Remove those two questions from the midterm question and grade just based on the first two questions, right? Well, he didn't. He said he would count the third one even if it's out of the syllabus. Absurd, right? He didn't even evaluate the project properly. There were no project demonstrations and presentations (we were literally confused about where we were heading). He only took the presentation slides as the submission.
His teaching is very poor, sorry to say. He used to read through the slides for most of the class. Even after finishing that course, I think I don't know a thing about NLP. If you are wondering I am sharing this review because I didn't get my expected grade, well, I got an A. So, if a student complains this much even after getting an A, just wonder how disastrous the course was?
If you are someone who is enthusiastic about learning pattern recognition and neural networks, don't waste your money by taking this course under his supervision. Do yourself a favor, and choose either SFM1, RTK, or NBM. But, if you are someone who just needs to get done with this course with a good grade with minimal effort, feel free to continue with him.
You're not gonna learn anything. But you might end up with a good grade.

For the exams, would recommend noting down practice question he gives out in class and demo questions for mids. You can the feed it into gpt to produce more practice questions.
Good to look common loss functions, cnns, etc and talking to gpt to learn the "whys". Also good to have a basic understanding of pruning, kd, other techniques as such and see how loss functions maybe written with properly symbols for these.
For the project: best to put together a reading list(papers) of the given topic with your teammates. Latest compilations can be found on github . When reading you can go through the abstract, if it looks interesting you can read the results + conclusion and limitations section.
Limitations sections are great. You can find your projects topic from a limitations section of a paper you like and you'll like be able to extend or use a paper's code on GitHub as a base to try your approach.
For the project idea, ask him to choose from multiple options, he'll provide inout on whats extendable and marketable on a paper potentially. For the demos, try to annoy him as much as possible till he defines what "deliverables" would look like for the next demo. I.e if x,y,z are done then that = 90-100 on the demo. Otherwise, it will get too stressful. Also when taking these notes from him on demos, if you show him too many ideas for the next one, he'll ask you to exectue on all ideas. Better to start off with x, then have him tell you some ideas off of that and not go to y unless he doesnt pitch in or says its not enough.

sva.review:
CSE465: Pattern Recognition & Neural Network
This is a good specialized course in the AI trail, giving you a solid understanding of Deep Learning. Although Machine Learning is not a prerequisite in the curriculum, having prior knowledge of ML definitely helps in understanding deep learning topics more easily. Prerequisites include Python, Statistics, LaTeX, and ideally some ML background.
I took it under SvA Ma’am. She followed the 100 Days of Deep Learning YouTube playlist for lectures. Throughout the semester, she covered three main architectures: Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN). In addition, the TA conducted two coding sessions on PyTorch.
The evaluation system included two quizzes (best one counted), one midterm, and one final exam. Most questions were based on the specific architectures, combining theory with mathematics. There were no assignments in this course. For the group project, the TA provided three domains, and students could pick one to propose their project idea. About two weeks were given for the project, so starting early is highly recommended. The project was evaluated by both the Maam and the TA. Overall, this course helps you gain specialization in Deep Learning, making it a valuable continuation after the Machine Learning course.
